card.band: 2 h. There are few levers, so a frontier agent usually succeeds. Credit comes from several levels and parameter paths. A weaker model finds the memset but not the row table.
card.cheat: Gating on exact output stops skipping compression. Hidden size and level mixes prevent tuning to one case.
card.grading: Gate: byte-identical output to the baseline for hidden inputs at levels 1-12 across all streaming API flows, plus the shipped tests. Medians of a hidden harness: tiny-input stream loops over sizes and levels. Reward is 2^u-1 against our reference.
card.reference: The upstream fix in PR #2969 plus the separate rowHash init fix, measured on the same harness.
card.source: https://github.com/facebook/zstd issue #2966 -> PR #2969, v1.5.1 vs v1.4.9, BSD-3-Clause
card.task: /app ships a history-less zstd v1.5.1 snapshot. Repeated ZSTD_compressStream on tiny inputs is up to 100x slower than in v1.4.9 (71 s against 0.5 s). The agent finds the causes in the context init and reset path (the lost lean init, the heavy rowHash table init) and fixes them without breaking compatibility.

source_notes: Levers: only 2 (restore lean context init that was lost in commit 980f3bbf; separate rowHash heavy initialization still to fix). Maintainer could not reproduce on silesia (v1.5.1 faster, 45.2 vs 36.5 MB/s), so benchmark must use tiny inputs with streaming API. Good as a short (2-4h) hidden-regression task rather than a long one. Reproducer source not opened: only issue text.
source_version: zstd v1.5.1 (regressed) vs v1.4.9 (good) -> zstd after PR #2969 (merged 2022-01-05, part 1) plus separate rowHash init fix

facts.claim: Issue #2966 exists and reports v1.4.9 vs v1.5.1 streaming slowdown: 512 ms vs 71,266 ms at level 10 (Windows, DLL build), about 139x

Seed's general claim that tiny-input streaming is up to 100x slower on v1.5.1 is reporter-specific: the maintainer could not reproduce the >100x gap and measured about 2.5x; the reporter's number is Windows-only
PR #2969 'fix performance issue in scenario #2966 (part 1)' exists and was merged into dev on Jan 5 2022 (merge commit 3c2c3fb)
PR #2969 restores the lean context init lost in commit 980f3bb, and the key change is in lib/compress/zstd_cwksp.h, described as a single-line change (later reworded in commit 41ad733)
The rowHash heavy initialization is NOT fixed by PR #2969; it was deferred to a separate follow-up (part 2, PR #2971 'do not initialize tag space', later closed)
The reference fix is large enough for the scale gate (hundreds of changed lines, at least 150 non-blank code lines)
Zstandard v1.5.1 release page exists; its listed changes do not mention streaming or context-init performance
Licence is BSD-style (three conditions: source and binary redistribution, non-endorsement, Meta copyright); the API spdx NOASSERTION is a detection artifact, and no patent grant appears in LICENSE
A public topic search found no separate v1.5.1-specific ZSTD_compressStream regression report beyond issue #2966

full_card.band: 2 h tier. Frontier agent probably finds the one lever in minutes; weaker model may find memset but not the rowHash table. Not a long-horizon scope.
full_card.build_cost: Under 1 day to build and write the harness; the ctest/junit mapping needs repair (amber).
full_card.deliverable: Patched lib/compress/ sources so repeated ZSTD_compressStream on tiny inputs regains v1.4.9-level speed at levels 1-12, with byte-identical output.
full_card.gates_anticheat: Byte-identical output gate across streaming flows stops skipping compression; hidden size and level mixes stop per-case tuning; tests and build config read-only.
full_card.grading_surface: Hidden timing harness (median wall-clock, tiny-input streaming loops over sizes and levels 1-12), byte-identity gate, plus shipped tests. Surface is modest: a few parameter paths.
full_card.local_fit: C, cmake, 8 cores, CPU only: fits. Smoke ctest parsed 0 tests and exited rc 8 on all 3 runs, so per-test results are missing.
full_card.lookup: partial: fix is public in upstream git history and later releases; history-less snapshot blocks git reading, but the one-line change is easily re-derived from the issue.
full_card.provenance: facebook/zstd issue #2966 -> PR #2969 (part 1, merged Jan 2022 into dev); rowHash part via PR #2971 (closed). Release v1.5.1 (Dec 2021 per release page). Pinned commit 49cf5179 per smoke probe.
full_card.reference: Upstream PR #2969 (lean init, one-line change in zstd_cwksp.h) plus the separate rowHash init fix. Reference is tiny; no complete implementation.
full_card.ships: History-less C snapshot of zstd v1.5.1 with the lean-init and rowHash init regressions present; cmake build ~13 s.
full_card.similarity: Nearest l0 neighbour S-op-006 at 0.371 (not a public task, but above the 0.15 bar). ProgramBench zstd 0.185. Not a crowded subject, but very narrow scope.

spike_plan.kill_if: Linux gap is under 2x (matches the maintainer's 2.5x), or the whole gain is a single line with no remaining headroom for multi-lever credit.
spike_plan.pass_if: Linux shows a gap of at least 5x between v1.5.1 and v1.4.9 on tiny streaming inputs, and the lean-init fix closes most of it with byte-identical output.
steps: In a throwaway Linux container with network, clone facebook/zstd at tag v1.5.1 (or the pinned commit) and build with cmake, -j4.
Write a tiny C harness that loops ZSTD_compressStream2 (or ZSTD_compressStream) over 11 to 1547 byte inputs at levels 1, 5, 10, 12 for 50,000 iterations and records median wall time.
Repeat on v1.4.9 with the same harness to measure the real gap on Linux.
Apply the PR #2969 lean-init change to v1.5.1 and re-measure; then apply the rowHash init fix and re-measure.
Check byte-identity of output across all levels between the patched and unpatched builds.
Record whether the gap is above 5x on Linux and whether the one-line fix closes most of it.

v1.summary: The source is real and confirmed: issue #2966 reports a Windows-only ~139x slowdown on v1.5.1, PR #2969 is a one-line lean-init fix, and the rowHash part was split into a follow-up PR. The seed fails the scale and long-horizon gates because the reference is far below 150 changed lines and the scope is two levers in a 2 h window, so kill with K10.
